body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across the Kalshi and Polymarket gold books — an empty list is the most common outcome from this scanner, and today is no exception. Nothing in either book currently offers a locked-in, fee-adjusted edge large enough for the tool to flag.

Spot gold is sitting in the low-$4,300s, with Kitco pegging it at $4,333.40 per troy ounce as of September 13, 2026, down $14.30 on the day, well off the all-time high of $5,589.38 reached on January 28, 2026. That level shows up cleanly in the contract structure: Kalshi's above $4,330.99 settlement contract for September 30 is priced almost exactly at a coin flip (47¢/51¢), which is exactly what you'd expect from a strike sitting right on top of the current spot price. Backdrop-wise, the market is digesting a hot inflation print — gold has been holding near $4,380 as hot August PPI lifted rate-hike odds toward 60% ahead of the Fed's September meeting — alongside strong investment demand, with the World Gold Council reporting gold ETFs took in $18 billion in August, pushing holdings to an all-time high of 4,189 tonnes.

Worth flagging for readers comparing the two platforms: Kalshi's contracts settle against a single price snapshot at a fixed date (e.g., 5pm EDT Sept 30), while most of Polymarket's gold contracts pay out if the price merely touches a level at any point during the window. That's why Polymarket's touch $4,300 contracts trade far richer (85¢/90¢) than Kalshi's equivalent settle-above strike — they're answering a different, easier-to-satisfy question, not offering free money. Any apparent cross-platform gaps in these listings are best read as differences in contract mechanics or thin order books rather than real edges.
headline: No arbitrage found between Kalshi and Polymarket gold books today
